# WordMeaning

> A free, open-source word-definition popup for Windows 10 and 11. It runs in the system tray;
> select a single word in any program and its definition appears at the cursor, then disappears
> after six seconds. About 86,000 WordNet 3.1 entries are compiled into the program, so lookups
> work with no internet connection. Nothing is written to disk.

Site: https://ishpreet36752.github.io/WordMeaning/
Source: https://github.com/ishpreet36752/WordMeaning (MIT licence)
Downloads (GitHub Releases, built in CI with a signed provenance attestation):
- Installer, ~4.5 MB: https://github.com/ishpreet36752/WordMeaning/releases/latest/download/WordMeaning-Setup.exe
- Portable single .exe, ~9 MB: https://github.com/ishpreet36752/WordMeaning/releases/latest/download/WordMeaning.exe

## Facts

- Platform: Windows 10 and 11 only. No macOS or Linux build (written in AutoHotkey v2).
- Price: free. MIT licence, no account, no ads, no paid tier, no telemetry, no API key.
- Gesture: double-click a word, or drag across it, in any program that allows text selection.
- Shows: the word, its part of speech, up to two meanings, and an example sentence when the
  dictionary has a plain one. Pronunciation and audio are deliberately never shown.
- Dismiss: click anywhere, switch windows, or wait six seconds.
- Offline: the dictionary ships inside the program; no request leaves the machine for a lookup.
  An optional tray switch checks missing words against an online dictionary. It is off by
  default, is session-only, and is never written to a config file.
- Privacy: looked-up words are held in memory for the session only. No history file, no log, no
  database. The clipboard is used to read the selection and is restored immediately afterwards,
  including when a lookup fails.
- Misses: a word the corpus lacks (proper nouns, brand names, very new slang) shows a miss plus
  a Ctrl+Shift+D hint that searches the web in your browser. The program never opens a browser
  on its own, and that hotkey is registered only while a popup is on screen.
- Install: per-user, no administrator rights. The portable .exe needs no install at all.
- SmartScreen warns on first launch because the binary is not code-signed. The releases carry a
  build provenance attestation instead: `gh attestation verify WordMeaning.exe --repo ishpreet36752/WordMeaning`.
- Data source: WordNet 3.1, Princeton University. WordNet 3.1 Copyright 2011 by Princeton
  University. All rights reserved.

## Limits

- English only, single words only. Phrases, idioms and multi-word selections are ignored.
- Fixed 2011 corpus: no proper nouns, no brand names, no recent slang.
- Scanned image-only PDFs have no text layer, so there is nothing to select.
- No thesaurus, no translation, no pronunciation audio.

## Pages

- https://ishpreet36752.github.io/WordMeaning/: what it is, a live demo of the gesture, downloads, FAQ.
- https://ishpreet36752.github.io/WordMeaning/offline-dictionary-windows.html: why and how the dictionary is bundled, and how to verify it works with no network.
- https://ishpreet36752.github.io/WordMeaning/look-up-words-while-reading.html: the setup, in four steps, for reading without tab switches.
- https://ishpreet36752.github.io/WordMeaning/dictionary-popup-for-pdf-windows.html: word lookup inside PDF readers, Word and Kindle for PC.
- https://ishpreet36752.github.io/WordMeaning/dictionary-popup-alternatives-windows.html: browser extension vs desktop dictionary vs website vs this, including where this one is the wrong choice.
